answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying weight to verified work, not key count. New keys queue at a public wharf, where each draws a different task from a shared garden of open problems, picked by hashing the key with the epoch beacon so answers can't be copied. Three random peers confirm each result before it credits that key's non-transferable ledger. Weight equals credits, so splitting the same work over 100 keys gives each 1/100 and gains nothing but 100 review fees. If a gale of keys reaches the wharf in one epoch, their credits vest twice as slowly. Limit: hired labor still counts.
